start.heading: Start
start.description: Prepare an account and an instance, then launch the game.
start.welcomeTitle: No instance is ready to launch
start.welcomeBody: Create an instance to download the game, then launch it with a signed-in account.
start.launchDisabled: Available after the first instance is installed

account.title: Account
account.body: Microsoft, offline and Yggdrasil identities are managed under Accounts.

instances.title: Instances
instances.body: Instances keep mods, worlds and Java settings isolated.

downloads.title: Downloads
downloads.body: Metadata, Java and content downloads will be queued here.

start.nextBody: This shell is the M1 deliverable. The next milestone makes the Vanilla path real.

metadata.title: Version metadata and Java
metadata.body: Resolve Mojang metadata, choose a matching runtime and verify every file.

instance.title: Atomic instance creation
instance.body: Stage the instance, verify all artifacts and commit only when everything succeeds.

launch.title: Launch to the main menu
launch.body: Build the argument array, stream logs and classify the exit.

start.readyBody: Minecraft {{version}} on {{loader}} is installed. The selected account signs in at the title screen.
start.launchNeedsAccount: Sign in to an account before launching.
start.instancesBody: The instances you launched most recently.

diagnosis.title: Diagnosis of the last run
diagnosis.body: The core reads the launch log, the newest crash report and how the process ended, and matches them against fixed rules. Nothing leaves this machine.
diagnosis.failed: The diagnosis could not be read.
diagnosis.truncated: The log is longer than the window that was read.
diagnosis.emptyBody: Nothing in the log matched a known failure. Read the log itself.
diagnosis.exportFailed: The bundle could not be written.
diagnosis.privacy: Paths, addresses, tokens and player names are masked before the bundle is written, so you can post it somewhere for help.

java-version-mismatch.title: Java is too old for this build
java-version-mismatch.fix: Pick a Java path matching the version the log asks for in General, or install a newer runtime from Downloads.

out-of-memory.title: The game ran out of memory
out-of-memory.fix: Raise the memory limit in settings, remove mods, or lower the render distance.

duplicate-mod.title: The same mod is installed twice
duplicate-mod.fix: Open Content, remove one copy of the file named in the evidence, and launch again.

missing-dependency.title: A mod is missing something it needs
missing-dependency.fix: Search Content for the library the log names and install it into this instance.

mixin-failure.title: A mod could not patch the game
mixin-failure.fix: The mod and the game or loader version do not line up. Update one of them to the same version.

class-loading-failure.title: A class could not be loaded
class-loading-failure.fix: Usually a mod built for another loader or version, or a core file left behind. Remove the file the evidence names.

loader-install-incomplete.title: The loader install is incomplete
loader-install-incomplete.fix: Install this instance again; the version file or its libraries is missing.

disk-full.title: There was no room left on disk
disk-full.fix: Free space on the drive holding the instance root, then install again.

permission-denied.title: A file could not be written
permission-denied.fix: Close whatever holds the folder open, and move the instance out of a folder that needs administrator rights.

network-failure.title: A download did not finish
network-failure.fix: Check the connection, choose another mirror in settings, and retry the download.

abnormal-exit.title: The process ended abnormally
abnormal-exit.fix: The game closed without a clean stop. Read the last lines of the log under the evidence.

crash-report-present.title: A crash report was written
crash-report-present.fix: Open it from the Logs pane; the cause section names the mod or world that failed.

unexplained-failure.title: No rule explained this run
unexplained-failure.fix: Nothing in the log matched a known failure. The log tail and the bundle are what someone needs to help.

instances.heading: Instances
instances.description: Each instance owns its game directory, mods, worlds, Java selection and logs.
instances.emptyBody: Create an instance, install its files and launch Minecraft from one place.
instances.noAccount: No account is signed in, so the game cannot start.
instances.exportBody: Export writes a portable manifest with the version, loader and content references so another installation can rebuild the instance.
instances.exportFailed: The manifest could not be exported.
instances.deleteBody: “{{name}}” and its whole directory, including mods and worlds, are removed. This cannot be undone.
instances.createBody: Pick a game version and an optional loader. Installation runs as a background task.
instances.name: Name
instances.idHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Used as the directory name.
instances.loaderVersionsFailed: Loader versions could not be loaded.
instances.versionsFailed: The version manifest could not be loaded. Check your connection.
instances.importBody: Paste a Mnelys instance manifest or choose a file exported from another installation.
instances.javaAuto: Automatic: use the managed runtime for this version
instances.logsBody: The process output of the most recent launch, kept in memory by the core.
instances.contentIntro: Installed files grouped by resource type. Removing one never touches another instance.
instances.installedEmptyBody: Mods, packs and shaders installed from a content platform appear here.
instances.logsFailed: The game log could not be read.
instances.needsAccount: Sign in first so the game has an identity.
instances.installQueued: Installation queued. Follow it in the task center.
instances.contentSearchPlaceholder: Filter by name or file name
instances.contentSearchAllKinds: Search covers every type, not only the selected tab.
instances.worldsBody: Worlds saved inside this instance folder, newest first.
instances.worldsEmptyBody: A world you save while this instance is running appears here.
instances.schematicsBody: Schematic files the Litematica, WorldEdit and similar mods write below the schematics folder.
instances.schematicsEmptyBody: Files saved to the schematics folder of this instance appear here.
instances.filesBody: Every file and folder inside the game directory of this instance.
instances.filesEmptyBody: Nothing has been written to this folder yet.
instances.filesTruncated: This folder holds more entries than are listed here.
instances.filesFolderNotice: Deleting a folder removes everything inside it.
instances.entriesUnavailable: The game directory of this instance does not exist yet. Install the instance first.
instances.logsFilesBody: Log and crash-report files this instance has written on disk.
instances.logsFileEmpty: No log file has been written yet.
instances.logsTruncated: Only the end of this file is read.
instances.entryConfirmBody: “{{name}}” is deleted from the instance folder. This cannot be undone.
instances.entryConfirmFolderBody: “{{name}}” and everything inside it are deleted. This cannot be undone.

downloads.heading: Downloads
downloads.description: One queue for metadata, Java runtimes, loaders and content.
downloads.emptyBody: Nothing is queued. Installs started from an instance appear here while they run.
downloads.queueBody: Background tasks owned by the core: metadata, Java, installs and content.

content.heading: Content
content.description: Search a platform, filter by version and loader, then install into the instance you picked.
content.browseBody: Results come from the selected platform and stay filtered by the resource type you pick.
content.noProviders: No content platform is configured. Modrinth is always available; CurseForge needs an API key.
content.emptyBody: Pick a resource type, then search the selected platform.
content.noInstances: Create an instance before installing content.

multiplayer.heading: Multiplayer
multiplayer.description: Terracotta rooms for playing with friends without opening a public port.
multiplayer.emptyBody: This page is reserved for room creation, members, relay status and diagnostics.
multiplayer.safetyBody: The local management endpoint will listen on loopback only, use a short-lived token and never open a public port automatically.

accounts.heading: Accounts
accounts.description: Microsoft, offline and external Yggdrasil identities share one account model.
accounts.signedOutBody: Credentials never enter the webview. The core will keep refresh tokens in the platform vault.

microsoft.title: Microsoft
microsoft.body: Official sign-in through the system browser with PKCE.

offline.title: Offline
offline.body: A clearly labelled local identity for testing and LAN play.

yggdrasil.title: External Yggdrasil
yggdrasil.body: Custom authentication with an explicit trust prompt.

accounts.removeBody: The stored credentials for this account are deleted from the system keyring. Player data on disk is not touched.
accounts.addDescription: Choose how this identity signs in. Tokens stay in the core and never reach the window.
accounts.offlineHint: An offline name is a local identity. Servers in online mode will not accept it.
accounts.yggdrasilHint: The password goes straight to the authentication server; only a token is stored in the keyring.
accounts.microsoftBody: Sign-in uses the Microsoft device-code flow in your browser. No password is typed into Mnelys.
accounts.microsoftCode: Enter this code on the Microsoft page:

developer.heading: Developer
developer.description: Bind a Gradle project to an instance, build, deploy and debug from one workspace.
developer.gateBody: Turn it on to reveal developer tools. The core keeps the same command boundary; the mode only changes the visible surface.
developer.enabledBody: These capabilities are scheduled after the launcher core is stable, starting with the M8 developer workspace.

build.title: Gradle build
build.body: Run the project wrapper and locate the built artifact.

debug.title: Debug run
debug.body: Deploy to the bound instance and attach JDWP.

daemon.title: Developer daemon
daemon.body: A loopback-only bridge for CLI and IDE clients.

developer.tasksBody: Everything the core is running right now, with cancellation.
developer.manifestBody: The Mojang manifest the installer resolves against. Mirrors never change the trust hash.
developer.manifestFailed: The version manifest could not be loaded.

settings.heading: Settings
settings.description: Appearance, language, downloads, developer tools and build facts.
settings.appearanceDescription: The window stays opaque on every platform. No Mica, Acrylic or vibrancy.
settings.accentDescription: Colours primary actions, selection and focus. The default is the Mnelys pink.
settings.accentAdjusted: The lightness was adjusted so text stays readable in this theme.
settings.languageDescription: Applies immediately and persists for this install.
settings.developerDescription: Shows the Developer section in the navigation. It does not grant additional core capabilities.
settings.aboutDescription: Mnelys installs Vanilla, Fabric, Quilt, Legacy Fabric, Forge and NeoForge, signs in with Microsoft, offline or Yggdrasil accounts, and installs content from Modrinth and CurseForge.
settings.iconsDescription: Every interface icon comes from Lucide (ISC). The application icon remains the Mnelys source artwork.
settings.coreDescription: Where the core keeps its data and how it reaches Mojang.
settings.mirrorDescription: Active route: {{active}}. Mirrors change transport only; every file is still checked against the original hash.
settings.memoryHint: Megabytes of heap for new launches. 0 lets the core decide. Allowed: 0 or 512–65536.
settings.memoryInvalid: Enter 0 or a value between 512 and 65536.
settings.rootDescription: Instances, caches and settings live here.
settings.loadFailed: Core settings could not be loaded.
settings.javaBody: Mnelys selects a managed runtime that matches the game version, or uses one you already have.
settings.javaInstallHint: Installing a major downloads a verified managed runtime in the background.
settings.javaFailed: Java runtimes could not be listed.
settings.javaEmpty: No Java runtime was detected yet. Install a managed one above.

tasks.title: Task center
tasks.description: Long-running work and this session's core log.
tasks.emptyBody: Long-running work will report its stage, speed, cancellation and retry state from the Rust core.
tasks.footer: The task center connects with the M2 vertical slice.

logs.emptyBody: Nothing has been recorded in this session yet. New entries appear here while the app runs.
logs.errorBody: The core did not return its log buffer. The rest of the shell keeps working.
logs.clearError: The core did not clear the log. Try again.
logs.confirmBody: This removes every entry from this session's in-memory log. It cannot be undone.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.coreUnavailable: The Mnelys core is not reachable. This usually means the desktop shell is not running the Rust backend.
error.coreNotImplemented: The core has not implemented that capability yet.
error.coreInvalidRequest: The core rejected the request as invalid.
error.coreConflict: That request conflicted with existing state.
error.coreInternal: The core reported an internal error.
